question: What is the primary advantage of parenteral medication administration over the oral route?

options.C: Elimination of the need for sterile technique
options.D: Lower risk of localized tissue trauma

explanation: Bypassing the gastrointestinal tract allows medications to enter the circulation and tissues directly for a rapid onset of action. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T13#GNS122_U2_T13_h1)

question: Which action demonstrates the correct application of safe medication principles prior to an injection?

options.A: Preparing medications for several patients simultaneously to save time
options.B: Verifying the prescription against the patient identity band multiple times
options.C: Relying entirely on family members to confirm drug allergies
options.D: Omitting hand hygiene if clean examination gloves are worn

explanation: Cross-checking the medication order with patient identifiers directly prevents administration errors in clinical practice. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T13#GNS122_U2_T13_h1)

question: Which injection site is currently recommended as the safest choice for intramuscular injections in adults?
explanation: The ventrogluteal site lacks major nerves and blood vessels, minimizing the risk of severe complications during deep muscle injections. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T13#GNS122_U2_T13_h2)

question: Why is the vastus lateralis muscle selected as the primary injection site for newborns and infants?

options.A: It is a large, well-developed muscle mass free of major nerve trunks.
options.B: It absorbs oily solutions faster than any other muscle group.
options.C: It is the only site that accepts volumes exceeding three milliliters.
options.D: It allows the infant to remain in a prone position easily.

explanation: Infants lack sufficient muscle mass in the gluteal and deltoid regions, making the thick thigh muscle the safest alternative. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T13#GNS122_U2_T13_h2)

question: What is the standard insertion angle for an intradermal skin test?
explanation: A shallow insertion angle ensures the medication remains within the dermal layer to form a visible bleb. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T13#GNS122_U2_T13_h3)

question: A patient requires a routine subcutaneous injection of insulin. Which angle and tissue depth combination is most appropriate?

options.A: Forty-five to ninety degrees into adipose tissue
options.B: Thirty degrees into a peripheral surface vein
options.C: Ninety degrees directly into deep muscle fibers
options.D: Fifteen degrees parallel to the epidermal surface

explanation: Subcutaneous injections target the fat layer beneath the dermis, utilizing a perpendicular or slightly angled approach depending on needle length and patient habitus. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T13#GNS122_U2_T13_h3)

question: Which needle gauge indicates the largest physical diameter?
explanation: Needle gauge operates on an inverse scale, where smaller numbers represent wider bores designed for rapid flow or viscous liquids. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T13#GNS122_U2_T13_h4)

question: What is the primary clinical purpose of engineered safety devices on injection needles?

options.A: To filter microscopic glass particles out of reconstituted drugs
options.B: To minimize accidental needlestick injuries for healthcare workers
options.C: To reduce the pain experienced by patients during skin puncture
options.D: To prevent the medication from leaking out of the syringe barrel

explanation: Safety shields and retractable designs physically block or cover the contaminated sharp immediately after use. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T13#GNS122_U2_T13_h4)

question: What specialized equipment should be used when drawing medication from a glass ampoule to protect the patient?
explanation: A filter needle traps microscopic glass shards that break off when snapping open an ampoule, preventing them from entering the syringe. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T13#GNS122_U2_T13_h5)

question: Why must air be injected into a closed medication vial prior to withdrawing the fluid?

options.A: To activate the chemical properties of the powdered drug
options.B: To sterilize the rubber diaphragm from surface bacteria
options.C: To aerate the solution and eliminate trapped bubbles
options.D: To create positive pressure that makes withdrawal easier

explanation: Injecting air replaces the volume of liquid being removed, preventing a vacuum from forming inside the rigid vial. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T13#GNS122_U2_T13_h5)

question: What is the correct action regarding skin antisepsis before inserting a needle?

options.A: Wipe the wet antiseptic away immediately with sterile gauze.
options.B: Apply the antiseptic in a back-and-forth scrubbing motion.
options.C: Blow forcefully on the skin to accelerate the drying process.
options.D: Allow the antiseptic to air-dry completely before puncture.

explanation: Antiseptics require adequate drying time to destroy surface microorganisms effectively and prevent chemical irritation upon insertion. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T13#GNS122_U2_T13_h6)

question: A student nurse prepares to administer an intramuscular injection. What is the correct technique for skin preparation at the selected site?

options.A: Wipe the area horizontally across the muscle fibers three separate times.
options.B: Cleanse in a circular motion starting from the center and moving outward.
options.C: Scrub vigorously from the outer edges toward the center injection spot.
options.D: Soak the skin surface with povidone-iodine for exactly five minutes.

explanation: Moving from the clean center to the dirtier periphery sweeps microorganisms away from the intended puncture site. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T13#GNS122_U2_T13_h6)

question: What is the primary clinical purpose of using the Z-track technique during an intramuscular injection?

options.A: To allow administration of larger volumes than the muscle can hold
options.B: To accelerate the systemic absorption rate of viscous oily solutions
options.C: To eliminate the need for skin antisepsis over bony prominences
options.D: To seal irritating medications deep within the muscle and prevent leakage

explanation: Displacing the skin prior to insertion creates a zigzag track that traps staining or irritating drugs within muscle tissue. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T13#GNS122_U2_T13_h7)

question: When should the displaced skin be released during a Z-track intramuscular injection?

options.A: Immediately before pushing the plunger to deliver the medication
options.B: After the needle has been completely withdrawn from the tissue
options.C: Before cleansing the skin surface with the alcoholic swab
options.D: While the needle is still resting inside the deep muscle layer

explanation: Releasing the skin only after needle withdrawal ensures the tissue shifts back and seals the needle tract completely. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T13#GNS122_U2_T13_h7)

question: What dangerous practice is a primary contributor to accidental occupational needlestick injuries?

options.A: Manual two-handed recapping of used needles
options.B: Disposing of uncapped sharps in rigid containers
options.C: Washing exposed skin with soap and running water
options.D: Using engineered safety shields on syringes

explanation: Trying to recap used needles with both hands frequently leads to accidental punctures of the fingers and palms. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T13#GNS122_U2_T13_h8)

question: Which nursing action is most effective in preventing localized muscle fibrosis and tissue necrosis in chronic injection patients?

options.A: Systematic rotation of injection sites across different anatomical zones
options.B: Always using the smallest gauge needle available on the hospital ward
options.C: Injecting medications rapidly to minimize exposure time in the tissue
options.D: Omitting skin antisepsis to prevent chemical irritation of the dermis

explanation: Rotating sites gives damaged tissue adequate time to heal, preventing fibrous scar tissue accumulation and poor drug absorption. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T13#GNS122_U2_T13_h8)

question: What critical details must be included in the nursing documentation after administering an injection?

options.A: Patient financial status and insurance verification numbers
options.B: Medication name, dose, route, site, date, time, and signature
options.C: The exact brand name of the antiseptic swab used on the skin
options.D: Detailed manufacturer serial numbers of the syringe barrel

explanation: Complete documentation proves that the medication was administered safely according to professional and legal standards. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T13#GNS122_U2_T13_h9)

question: Why is immediate post-procedure patient monitoring particularly vital after administering a first-time antibiotic injection?

options.A: To detect acute hypersensitivity reactions and life-threatening anaphylaxis early
options.B: To confirm that the patient can swallow oral medications independently
options.C: To measure the exact reduction in body temperature within five minutes
options.D: To prevent the patient from walking around the ward too quickly

explanation: Severe allergic reactions can develop rapidly after parenteral drug exposure, requiring immediate emergency intervention. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T13#GNS122_U2_T13_h9)
